Chlorophyll Sweeper.description:
• Venusaur, due to its ability in Chlorophyll and excellent coverage, is a strong offensive threat in the metagame. These traits are complemented by Venusaur's access to Sleep Powder, which lets it put threats it and its partners struggle with like Garchomp and Aerodactyl to sleep.

  • Earth Power versus Grass-type Coverage: Earth Power deals with Steel-types like Archaludon and Kingambit that resist its STAB moves. This coverage pairs well with its best partner in Mega Charizard Y, as Earth Power also deals with Rock- and Fire-types that Mega Charizard Y struggles to deal with, such as Glimmora and Blaziken. However, if the rest of the team is able to handle these threats, Grass-type coverage may be used instead.

  • Sleep Powder versus Grass-type coverage: Sleep Powder has shaky accuracy but makes Venusaur especially terrifying. This is because Venusaur's boosted Speed under the sun lets it shut down checks like Mega Staraptor and Incineroar. If Venusaur is using Life Orb, a third move in Solar Beam or Leaf Storm is preferred to take advantage of the damage boost.

  • Solar Beam versus Leaf Storm: Solar Beam gives Venusaur a more spammable STAB move. When boosted by Helping Hand, Solar Beam OHKOes Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl. On the other hand, Leaf Storm OHKOes threats like Milotic regardless of the weather at the cost of dropping Venusaur's Special Attack.

  • Abilities: Chlorophyll boosts Venusaur's Speed under the sun, letting it outspeed Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon, Sneasler, and Mega Aerodactyl and put these threats to sleep or heavily damage them.

  • Items: Focus Sash makes Sleep Powder's inaccuracy easier to handle, as it lets Venusaur at least have another chance to put a foe to sleep in case it misses. Focus Sash can also be crucial to let Venusaur deal some damage or inflict sleep in case the opponent sets up Tailwind. Alternatively, Life Orb boosts Venusaur's damage, letting it take out most Pelipper with Leaf Storm and non-bulky Mega Floette with Sludge Bomb.

Other Options

  • Protect versus a Third Attacking Move: Protect may be dropped in favor of a third attacking move to maximize Venusaur's offensive capabilities, as Venusaur will generally go first under the sun and put an opposing threat to sleep or finish it off before it can attack. Furthermore, Venusaur has decent bulk, surviving hits from Kingambit, Archaludon, Garchomp, and can have extra insurance if it's using a Focus Sash. However, dropping Protect leaves it vulnerable to Fake Out disruption.

  • Energy Ball: Energy Ball is not dependent on the weather and does not drop Venusaur's Special Attack while still doing enough damage to remove Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert. However, this leaves Venusaur unable to OHKO bulky Basculegion-M.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: While Venusaur can invalidate most of its offensive checks with Sleep Powder, it can find itself in an extremely bad situation if Sleep Powder misses. Venusaur also fails to OHKO most threats like Mega Staraptor, Mega Metagross, and Hydreigon even with the Life Orb boost and will get OHKOed back.

  • Bulkier Steel- and Grass-types like Gholdengo and Mega Venusaur give problems to Venusaur, as they shrug off its attacks. If Venusaur is lacking Earth Power, Gholdengo can even use it as setup fodder and OHKO it with +2 Make it Rain.

  • Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales, Mega Tyranitar, and Pelipper can swap in and shut down Venusaur's ability, allowing their teammates to outspeed and remove it.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is Venusaur's best partner, as it sets sun to activate Chlorophyll and deals with Steel- and Grass-types that Venusaur struggles with, such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Mega Venusaur.

  • Tailwind setters such as Aerodactyl and Whimsicott provide an extra Speed boost to match opposing teams' Tailwind. Aerodactyl also deals with opposing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, while Whimsicott provides more disruption in Encore and can also use Fake Tears to allow Venusaur to pick up surprise OHKOs.

  • Incineroar helps Venusaur put a foe to sleep more safely by using Fake Out, and it also deals with Mega Metagross and Gholdengo.

  • An alternative sun setter in Torkoal may be considered, as it frees up the Mega Evolution slot and allows the rest of the team to utilize other modes of play, such as Trick Room. Torkoal also provides Helping Hand support, which allows Venusaur to OHKO Archaludon, Mega Metagross, and Garchomp.

Sun Sweeper.description:
• Mega Charizard Y is a ruthless sweeper dealing immense damage with its Fire-type attacks. It threatens OHKOs and 2HKOs on the majority of the metagame such as Mega Floette, Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Mega Metagross. Mega Charizard Y opts to run bulk rather than maximizing its offense and Speed to help it survive longer in contrast to Regulation M-A.

  • Three Attacks Sweeper: Mega Charizard Y dominates simply using three attacks: Heat Wave, Weather Ball, and Solar Beam. Heat Wave provides powerful spread Fire-type damage. Weather Ball deals insane Fire-type damage while sun is active or provides handy coverage depending on the weather, and it is unaffected by Wide Guard. Solar Beam is necessary to threaten Water-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert.

  • Drought: The sun set by Drought increases the damage of Mega Charizard Y's Fire-type attacks, guaranteeing that Heat Wave will OHKO Kingambit and Sinistcha. It also allows Solar Beam to be used in a single turn, enables Venusaur's Chlorophyll, and reduces the damage of Wave Crash from Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert.

  • Mega Evolving Charizard: Mega Charizard Y should not Mega Evolve right away unless there are no foes that can override the sun. It is best to wait until the opponent has sent out or Mega Evolved their weather setter like Pelipper and Mega Froslass before Mega Evolving Mega Charizard Y to ensure sun is not overridden.

Other Options

  • Helping Hand: Helping Hand can be run over Solar Beam when Mega Charizard Y is paired with Venusaur. Helping Hand-boosted Solar Beam from Life Orb Venusaur OHKOs Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl, dealing significantly more damage than Mega Charizard Y's own Solar Beam.

  • Ancient Power: Ancient Power is a niche move used instead of Solar Beam primarily as a surprise attack to OHKO opposing Mega Charizard Y and to let it threaten Ceruledge and Hisuian Arcanine. An omni boost from Ancient Power is also extremely beneficial for Mega Charizard Y, letting it survive Rock Slide and giving it a chance to OHKO Mega Floette with Weather Ball.

SP Spreads

  • 16 HP / 25 Def / 12 SpA / 13 Spe with Modest: The given spread lets Mega Charizard Y survive Rock Slide from non-Life Orb Garchomp and gives it a good chance to survive Mystic Water-boosted Wave Crash from Adaptability Jolly Basculegion-M in the sun. 13 Speed SPs let Mega Charizard Y outspeed maximum Speed Modest Venusaur without active Chlorophyll, and the remaining SPs are invested into Special Attack to maximize Mega Charizard Y's damage output.

  • 30 HP / 31 Def / 1 SpA / 4 Spe with Modest: This bulkier SP spread provides Mega Charizard Y with a high chance to survive Rock Slide from Life Orb-boosted Jolly Garchomp and Aerodactyl and grants a favorable chance to survive Wave Crash from Life Orb-boosted Adaptability Basculegion-M in the sun. The Speed investment ensures Mega Charizard Y outruns Adamant Mega Swampert and Mega Tyranitar in the sun, and the remaining SPs are put into Special Attack.

  • 16 HP / 17 Def / 10 SpA / 23 Spe with Timid: This faster SP spread allows Mega Charizard Y to outspeed Excadrill in the sun as well as Glimmora and Hisuian Arcanine. The defensive investment allows Mega Charizard Y to survive Rock Slide from -1 Lycanroc-D, and the leftover SPs maximize Mega Charizard Y's Special Attack.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Charizard Y's biggest adversaries are Rock-types such as Mega Tyranitar, Mega Aerodactyl, Lycanroc-D, and Glimmora. They all easily threaten OHKOs with Rock Slide, Accelerock, and Power Gem respectively while Mega Charizard Y struggles to KO them.

  • Mega Raichu Y outspeeds Mega Charizard Y and easily threatens an OHKO with Zap Cannon.

  • Rain teams are difficult for Mega Charizard Y to defeat. Rain significantly reduces the damage of Heat Wave and Solar Beam, and it enables Mega Swampert's Swift Swim, allowing it to outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Wave Crash. Pelipper, Archaludon, and Sinistcha are also difficult for Mega Charizard Y to remove while rain is active. Pelipper and Archaludon threaten to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Weather Ball and Electro Shot, respectively. Sinistcha can also set up Trick Room, allowing Pelipper and Archaludon to attack first, and it can provide them with redirection as well as healing thanks to Hospitality.

  • Although Mega Charizard Y can survive their attacks, Garchomp and Basculegion-M are still threats to it. Mega Charizard Y is naturally outrun by Garchomp and is unable to KO it with Solar Beam before Garchomp attacks twice with Rock Slide. Basculegion-M can outspeed Mega Charizard Y with Tailwind support from Whimsicott, giving Basculegion-M an opportunity to KO Mega Charizard Y before it can attack.

  • While it is an uncommon pick, Ceruledge walls all of Mega Charizard Y's attacks, so it can easily take advantage of this to set up with Bulk Up and proceed to snowball.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp and Basculegion-M are Mega Charizard Y's best partners, easily threatening Rock-types and Ceruledge as well as opposing Garchomp and Basculegion-M. Garchomp in particular can remove Mega Raichu Y. They are also great at pressuring opposing Mega Charizard Y.

  • While Mega Floette cannot be used in the same battle as Mega Charizard Y, it synergizes well as an alternative Mega Evolution when Mega Charizard Y has an unfavorable matchup. Mega Floette is great at removing Garchomp and deals devastating damage to Pokemon commonly found on rain teams like Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Archaludon. In return, Mega Charizard Y can easily threaten Mega Metagross, Gholdengo, Mega Gengar, and Mega Mawile, all of which Mega Floette is threatened by.

  • Incineroar is great at providing damage mitigation with Intimidate, ensuring that Mega Charizard Y survives Rock Slide from the Rock-types and Garchomp. It also provides Fake Out support to let Mega Charizard Y dish out damage safely.

  • Venusaur threatens Mega Aerodactyl and Garchomp, which Mega Charizard Y struggles to damage, as well as common Water-types like Basculegion-M, Mega Blastoise, and Mega Swampert. Sleep Powder can also disrupt foes, letting Mega Charizard Y stick around for longer.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Mega Blaziken's high Speed and Attack give it a good matchup against metagame staples like Incineroar, Kingambit, and Gholdengo. With Speed Boost, it can essentially guarantee it is the fastest Pokemon on the field after enough turns have passed, outspeeding Mega Aerodactyl and slower Pokemon like Sylveon even if they have a boost from Tailwind.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide OHKOes Mega Charizard Y. Combined with Speed Boost, Rock Slide lets Mega Blaziken threaten flinches before foes can move.

  • Detect: Detect is mandatory to safely gain Speed boosts.

Other Options

  • Swords Dance: Swords Dance can be used to offset Intimidate from Incineroar and make Mega Blaziken strong enough to OHKO Garchomp with Close Combat at +1 Attack. It can replace Rock Slide on teams that have another way to cover Mega Charizard Y, such as Mega Aerodactyl.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: Speed Boost allows Adamant Mega Blaziken to outspeed Mega Aerodactyl after one turn.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Opting for a Jolly nature allows Mega Blaziken to always outspeed Sylveon under Tailwind after one turn.

Teambuilding

  • Rain Matchup: Mega Swampert threatens to OHKO Mega Blaziken with either STAB attack, and Swift Swim lets it outspeed Mega Blaziken in the rain even after a turn of Speed Boost. Basculegion-M and Pelipper resist both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks and respond with an OHKO from Wave Crash and Hurricane or Weather Ball, respectively; Pelipper also weakens Flare Blitz while enabling Mega Swampert with Drizzle.

  • Other Weaknesses: Garchomp threatens an OHKO with Earthquake, which cannot be redirected by Sinistcha's Rage Powder. Mega Aerodactyl threatens an OHKO with Dual Wingbeat and can use Tailwind before Mega Blaziken gets its Speed Boost to deny Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage. Whimsicott has Tailwind to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage and Encore to punish it for using Detect to gain Speed Boosts. Opposing Trick Room uses Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost against it, and Farigiraf threatens to OHKO it with Psychic. Mega Staraptor enters the field with Intimidate, threatens an OHKO with Brave Bird, and is often paired with Whimsicott to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost with Tailwind. Mega Delphox threatens an OHKO with Psychic or Psyshock. Ceruledge completely walls both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M has a better matchup against rain teams and Mega Aerodactyl, while Mega Blaziken helps it against Archaludon. Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales and Torkoal overwrite rain; Alolan Ninetales handles Garchomp with Blizzard; and Torkoal is useful in Trick Room while providing sun to let Flare Blitz OHKO bulky variants of Sylveon and offensive variants of Farigiraf. Sinistcha can nearly OHKO Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha and use Rage Powder to redirect threatening attacks like Pelipper's Weather Ball and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. It can also redirect neutral attacks that threaten Mega Blaziken due to its low bulk, like Sneasler's Dire Claw and Close Combat. Sinistcha helps offset Flare Blitz recoil with Hospitality and can also reverse Trick Room. Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Kingambit, which threatens Sinistcha.

  • Kingambit threatens to OHKO Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch and is comfortable against Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge, as it can survive their attacks and either OHKO them in return or deal enough damage to finish them off with Sucker Punch. Due to Defiant, Kingambit's presence can also deter Incineroar from switching in and activating Intimidate against Mega Blaziken. In return, Mega Blaziken handles Mega Charizard Y for Kingambit with Rock Slide. Sylveon is a strong answer to Garchomp, and Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Steel-types that threaten Sylveon, such as Gholdengo and Mega Metagross.

  • Alternative Mega Evolutions: Mega Aerodactyl can take the place of Mega Blaziken against teams with nuisances like Garchomp, Mega Delphox, Ceruledge, and opposing Mega Aerodactyl. Mega Blaziken complements Mega Aerodactyl by beating its counters: Mega Tyranitar, Mega Metagross, and Mega Mawile. Mega Froslass has a better matchup against rain teams by setting snow over rain, and it is also strong against Garchomp and the combination of Mega Staraptor and Whimsicott. Mega Blaziken also plays well against Mega Froslass's counters: Mega Charizard Y, Kingambit, and Incineroar.

Fast Offense.description:
• Mega Swampert gives rain teams a clear choice of Mega Evolution, using its newly granted access to Wave Crash to hit incredibly hard. It is able to OHKO most Pokemon in Regulation M-B that do not resist Wave Crash in rain, albeit at the cost of a large portion of its own HP. It boasts a strong matchup against Regulation M-B staples such as Incineroar, Mega Metagross, and Sneasler.

  • Swift Swim: Swift Swim allows Mega Swampert to outrun every unboosted Pokemon in the tier when rain is active. This means it outspeeds the likes of Garchomp and Mega Raichu Y, two Pokemon that would otherwise greatly burden its partners. Mega Swampert can OHKO them before Garchomp threatens partner Archaludon with Earthquake or Mega Raichu Y threatens Archaludon and Pelipper with Focus Blast and Zap Cannon, respectively.

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch allows Mega Swampert to threaten the Grass-types that OHKO it, such as Sinistcha, as well as Garchomp, which would otherwise deal a large amount of damage to Mega Swampert through the combination of Wave Crash recoil and Rough Skin contact damage. Notably, it is able to OHKO Whimsicott after Fake Out breaks its Focus Sash, preventing it from setting Tailwind and allowing Mega Swampert to maintain its Speed advantage in rain. It also allows Mega Swampert to hit the occasional Mega Dragonite for heavy damage.

  • Ground-type moves: While some Mega Swampert opt to run only Earthquake, others run High Horsepower to hit Steel-types such as Kingambit without threatening their partner. High Horsepower can be run instead of Earthquake, replacing it as the only Ground-type move, or instead of Ice Punch, forgoing coverage.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Swampert heavily relies on rain to boost its damage output and Speed. Without it, Mega Swampert can struggle to survive specific attacks such as Solar Beam from Mega Charizard Y or secure certain OHKOs. As such, one of its most problematic foes is Mega Charizard Y. If Mega Charizard Y catches Mega Swampert in sun, it can outspeed and OHKO it with Solar Beam, while Mega Swampert cannot OHKO bulky Mega Charizard Y in sun even after surviving Solar Beam.

  • Grass-type threats: Sinistcha can also be a problem, as Mega Swampert struggles to even 2HKO physically bulky Sinistcha with Ice Punch, while Sinistcha can threaten massive damage to Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha and is immune to Fake Out and Rage Powder. Venusaur is also able to survive Ice Punch and retaliate with Giga Drain or another Grass-type move.

  • Basculegion-M: Basculegion-M can take advantage of Mega Swampert's preferred weather and threaten an OHKO with rain-boosted Wave Crash while avoiding an OHKO from High Horsepower or Earthquake.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Swampert synergizes well with Archaludon, as Mega Swampert is able to outspeed and OHKO Archaludon's biggest counters in Garchomp, Mega Raichu Y, and Sneasler, while Archaludon resists the Grass-type moves that threaten Mega Swampert. Archaludon can also take Wave Crash from Basculegion-M and retaliate with Electro Shot in rain while bolstering its Defense with Stamina. However, both Pokemon heavily rely on the weather being in their favor to successfully win these matchups.

  • Drizzle Pokemon: Mega Swampert is run exclusively on teams featuring either Pelipper or Politoed, as it is simply not worth using unless it is on a rain-focused team. It is usually run with Pelipper, as Pelipper can threaten the Grass-types that threaten Mega Swampert with Hurricane while being immune to Mega Swampert's Earthquake.

  • Dual screens setters: Mega Swampert is often paired with Grimmsnarl or Sableye, as their Light Screen and Reflect help Archaludon and Mega Swampert stay on the field. Using Rain Dance with Sableye guarantees that rain will be active that turn, as Sableye moves after Mega Charizard YMega Evolves or switches in and sets sun.

  • Redirection: Sinistcha helps Mega Swampert's common partner Archaludon with its Ground-type resistance and ability to set Trick Room, allowing Archaludon to move before threats such as Garchomp. On top of that, Sinistcha can quickly dispatch opposing Mega Swampert, a matchup that can be volatile for Mega Swampert and partner Archaludon. It is also able to redirect and resist Wave Crash from Basculegion-M.

Fast Sweeper.description:
• Mega Metagross boasts good stats and a very beneficial ability in Tough Claws, which allow it to spearhead entire matchups with its raw single-target damage while taking out its checks with its various coverage moves. Mega Metagross's useful Steel typing lets it take on the format's Fairy-type Pokemon such as Sylveon and Mega Floette with ease.

  • Iron Head vs. Bullet Punch: On teams without prominent speed control, Bullet Punch is an alternative to Iron Head that allows Mega Metagross to secure a KO on faster Pokemon at low health, such as Aerodactyl, Whimsicott, and Sneasler after activating Focus Sash.

  • Body Press vs. Ice Punch vs. Stomping Tantrum: These moves allow Mega Metagross to beat Kingambit and Incineroar, Garchomp, and Ceruledge, respectively. Choosing a coverage move largely depends on how well Mega Metagross's partners perform against these Pokemon. For example, if Mega Metagross is partnered with a Garchomp, opting for Ice Punch can help Garchomp consistently win a mirror matchup without relying on a Speed tie, while Garchomp already covers Kingambit with Earthquake.

  • Mega Evolving Metagross: With Clear Body, Metagross is able to shrug off Intimidate from Incineroar. As such, if the opponent has an Incineroar, it is wise to delay Metagross's Mega Evolution until Metagross actually attacks or Incineroar has already switched in, as this prevents Incineroar from easily lowering Mega Metagross's Attack stat.

SP Spreads

  • 27 Atk / 14 Def / 25 Spe with Jolly: Generally, this SP spread is only worth running if Mega Metagross is also using Body Press. The Defense investment allows it to always OHKO Kingambit with Body Press, while the Speed investment allows it to always outspeed Garchomp and Mega Floette.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: This SP spread is used when Mega Metagross is running either Stomping Tantrum or Ice Punch, as Body Press cannot consistently OHKO Kingambit without any Defense investment and is thus not worth running. The extra Attack investment allows it to almost always 2HKO uninvested Basculegion-M with Psychic Fangs, even at -1. The Speed investment allows Mega Metagross to outspeed Alolan Ninetales, letting Metagross OHKO it with Iron Head.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Metagross relies on outspeeding and OHKOing its checks. Basculegion-M poses a problem for this gameplan, as Mega Metagross cannot OHKO it with Psychic Fangs, while Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed Mega Metagross and threaten an OHKO with 100-Base Power Last Respects. Mega Metagross can beat non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M only if a partner chips it beforehand.

  • Other Mega Evolutions: Mega Delphox resists both of Mega Metagross's STAB moves while outspeeding Mega Metagross and threatening heavy damage with Heat Wave. Bulky Mega Gengar can threaten a KO on Mega Metagross with Shadow Ball after some chip damage while outspeeding it. Mega Swampert can take any attack from Mega Metagross and has a slight chance to OHKO it with High Horsepower or Earthquake, as well as outspeeding it if the rain is up. Mega Charizard Y is also able to survive Psychic Fangs and can retaliate with sun-boosted Heat Wave or Weather Ball, OHKOing Mega Metagross.

  • Coverage Move Trade-offs: As Mega Metagross cannot fit all of its coverage moves onto its set, it is important to be aware of Metagross's negative matchups depending on the selected coverage option and take these into account when building around Metagross.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Metagross is often used on rain teams, as Drizzle or Rain Dance can make Mega Charizard Y reposition or allow Mega Metagross to survive a Heat Wave or Weather Ball. Common rain staples such as Mega Swampert also boast an excellent matchup against Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, and Mega Charizard Y. Additionally, Ice Punch Mega Metagross can cover Garchomp, which would otherwise threaten Archaludon, a rain staple.

  • Mega Metagross as a Matchup Fixer: On other teams, such as those with Mega Charizard Y, Mega Metagross can be used as a secondary Mega Evolution option to handle foes such as Toxapex and opposing weather setters like Mega Tyranitar and Mega Froslass.

Fast Attacker.description:
• Garchomp, thanks to its strong offense, good coverage against the current format's major threats, and nice Speed tier, cements itself as a top threat in Regulation M-B, offensively checking the likes of Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, Incineroar, and Kingambit with ease.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide allows Garchomp to threaten Flying-type Pokemon, namely Mega Charizard Y and Mega Aerodactyl. It can also deal considerable damage to Mega Delphox and is Garchomp's only way to hit Whimsicott, which are immune to Earthquake and resist it, respectively. Rock Slide, thanks to Garchomp's high Speed, can be used to fish for flinches, though it is generally an unreliable path to victory.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb allows Garchomp to always OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide and OHKO opposing Garchomp with Dragon Claw.

  • Rough Skin: Rough Skin allows Garchomp to punish Fake Out from the likes of Sneasler and Incineroar, while also breaking the Focus Sash of physical attackers such as Kingambit, Sneasler, and Basculegion-M.

Other Options

  • Stomping Tantrum: Stomping Tantrum can be run on teams that don't have many Earthquake-immune Pokemon, allowing Garchomp to deal consistent Ground-type damage without threatening its partners. This comes at the cost of either Earthquake or Rock Slide, either limiting Garchomp's offensive capabilities or preventing it from OHKOing Mega Charizard Y.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Ice-type Pokemon like Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales threaten big damage with Blizzard and can lessen Garchomp's damage output with Aurora Veil. Pokemon that commonly run Ice-type coverage, like Mega Metagross and Mega Swampert, also cause issues, as both can outspeed Garchomp — whether it be naturally or through Swift Swim — and OHKO it with Ice Punch, while Mega Swampert is also bulky enough to tank two Dragon Claws. Mega Aerodactyl can do similarly with Ice Fang.

  • Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten Garchomp with Moonblast and Hyper Voice, while Mega Floette has the chance to Speed tie with Garchomp. Whimsicott in particular is problematic, as it is also resistant to Ground-type attacks and can use Tailwind to allow Pokemon that Garchomp usually outspeeds, like Sylveon and most Mega Floette, to KO it before it can move.

  • Mega Scovillain provides issues for Garchomp, easily redirecting its attacks and burning it. Incineroar can also weaken Garchomp with Intimidate, while Fake Out significantly hinders Garchomp's potential momentum.

  • Opposing Dragon-type Pokemon like Choice Scarf Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite can either outspeed Garchomp or withstand it for a turn and OHKO it with Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is immune to Garchomp's Earthquake and pressures Ice- and Fairy-type Pokemon with Weather Ball, OHKOing the Ice-type Pokemon and outdamaging the Fairy-types. Mega Charizard Y also threatens Mega Metagross with Weather Ball or Heat Wave and, when the sun is up, Mega Swampert with Solar Beam. Mega Charizard Y can also pressure Mega Scovillain without fear of being burnt. Garchomp, in return, hits the many Rock-type Pokemon that threaten Mega Charizard Y, like Mega Tyranitar and Glimmora, with Earthquake while also threatening opposing Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide.

  • Whimsicott provides Tailwind, allowing Garchomp to outspeed other Garchomp as well as Hydreigon and threaten to OHKO them with Dragon Claw. Moonblast can also be used to threaten Dragon-type Pokemon, as a double target with Moonblast and Dragon Claw OHKOes Mega Dragonite. In return, Garchomp pressures the likes of Gholdengo and Kingambit, which would otherwise threaten Whimsicott with Make It Rain and Iron Head, respectively.

  • Kingambit threatens Ice- and Fairy-type Pokemon with Iron Head, while both it and Basculegion-M threaten Incineroar with Low Kick and Wave Crash, respectively.

Sun Attacker.description:
• Mega Pyroar is a devastating sun attacker in Regulation M-B, taking advantage of Fire Mane and the sun to deal monstrous amounts of damage. Mega Pyroar's typing makes it immune to Basculegion-M's Last Respects and resistant to Gholdengo's and Mega Charizard Y's main STAB attacks as well as Fairy-type attacks from Mega Floette, Mega Gardevoir, and Sylveon.

  • Overheat: Overheat allows Mega Pyroar to OHKO nearly everything in the metagame with enough damage multipliers, including Pokemon that may resist Overheat, such as Incineroar and Garchomp.

  • Solar Beam: Solar Beam is used to hit Water-types like Basculegion-M, Mega Blastoise, and Mega Swampert for super effective damage.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Pelipper and Politoed can decrease Mega Pyroar's damage output with Drizzle while threatening it with rain-boosted Weather Ball. Rain allows Mega Swampert to outspeed and threaten Mega Pyroar with either STAB attack while denying Solar Beam as a coverage option.

  • Focus Sash Sneasler can survive one attack from Mega Pyroar and OHKO it back with Close Combat. Unburden-boosted Sneasler can also outspeed and OHKO Mega Pyroar. Sneasler's Fake Out can also slow down Mega Pyroar's momentum.

  • Garchomp and Basculegion-M resist Mega Pyroar's Fire-type moves while threatening to OHKO it with Life Orb-boosted Earthquake and Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash, respectively.

  • Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed Mega Pyroar, survive a sun- and Fire Mane-boosted Overheat, block Heat Wave with Wide Guard, 2HKO Mega Pyroar with Rock Slide, and set up Tailwind for other Mega Pyroar checks such as Garchomp to outspeed it. Mega Tyranitar can shut off the sun, reducing Mega Pyroar's damage output while resisting its Fire-type attacks and threatening it with Rock Slide.

  • Ceruledge soaks up Mega Pyroar's Fire-type attacks while resisting Solar Beam. Ceruledge also takes advantage of the sun while setting up with Bulk Up in the face of Mega Pyroar. Notably, at +1 Attack, Bitter Blade in the sun 2HKOes Mega Pyroar.

  • Choice Scarf Hydreigon resists all of Mega Pyroar's moves while outspeeding it and weakening it with Snarl or threatening it with Earth Power. Mega Dragonite also resists all of Mega Pyroar's moves while setting up Tailwind in its face and chunking it with Dragon Pulse.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Torkoal enables Mega Pyroar's immense damage output with Drought. It also provides a Trick Room mode with Farigiraf as well as Helping Hand support, allowing Mega Pyroar to OHKO no-bulk Garchomp and Impish Incineroar with Overheat and 2HKO most Mega Charizard Y sets with Heat Wave if sun is up.

  • Farigiraf nullifies Fake Out, preventing it from stalling out Mega Pyroar's sun turns or disrupting its momentum, and can set up Trick Room for Mega Pyroar's partner Torkoal. Farigiraf can OHKO Sneasler through Focus Sash with Twin Beam and threaten Water-types like Pelipper, Politoed, and Basculegion-M with Thunderbolt.

  • Venusaur threatens Basculegion-M with Solar Beam and can put foes to sleep with Sleep Powder. Whimsicott gives Mega Pyroar speed control with Tailwind and weather control with Sunny Day. Whimsicott resists both of Garchomp's STAB attacks while chunking it with Moonblast. Vileplume also utilizes Sleep Powder but has access to After You, allowing allied Torkoal to fire off Eruption almost immediately. However, Vileplume is forced to run Focus Sash and does not hit as hard as Venusaur.

  • Mega Floette can threaten the Dragon-types that may hinder Mega Pyroar with Fairy Aura-boosted Dazzling Gleam and Moonblast.

Defensive Support.description:
• Toxapex finds itself serving a unique role within the Regulation M-B metagame as a supportive wall thanks to its valuable Water / Poison dual typing and sky-high defensive stats. These allow it to sit in front of and greatly limit offensive threats such as Mega Charizard Y, Garchomp, and Sylveon.

  • Infestation: Infestation enables Toxapex to provide some level of offensive pressure along with trapping foes on the field, messing up attempts to reposition.

  • Wide Guard: Wide Guard can protect Toxapex and teammates like Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit from spread moves such as Rock Slide and Earthquake.

  • Toxic: Toxic forces timers onto foes such as Milotic and Mega Staraptor, preventing them from being able to setup and win games safely.

  • Infestation, Toxic, and Baneful Bunker Synergy: This trio of moves synergizes well with each other and turns Toxapex into an active threat, as the combination of Infestation and poison does immense amounts of damage over time, softening up foes for partners to KO them.

  • Regenerator: Regenerator helps keep Toxapex healthy throughout a match to let it maintain pressure with trapping and spreading poison.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 16 Def / 18 SpD with Bold: This spread allows Toxapex to take Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M's 200-Base Power Last Respects at full HP in addition to Mega Delphox's Psychic.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Toxapex can be greatly annoyed by Steel- and Poison-types, as their immunity to Toxic prevents them from being worn down quickly and leaves Toxapex with only Infestation to whittle away at them. Archaludon, Mega Metagross, and Venusaur can prove especially problematic for Toxapex because they can also threaten it with powerful attacks like Electro Shot, Psychic Fangs, and Earth Power. Psychic- and Ground-types such as Mega Delphox, Farigiraf, and Mega Swampert, while not immune to Toxic, can still scare Toxapex through their STAB moves.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y greatly appreciates Toxapex's Wide Guard blocking Rock Slide from Garchomp and Aerodactyl, and in return, it can melt through Steel-types such as Kingambit and Gholdengo.

  • Kingambit and Incineroar can prey on the Psychic-types that break Toxapex like Mega Delphox and Farigiraf, and they also can deal with Ghost-types such as Mega Gengar and Sinistcha, which can escape Infestation's Bound effect. In return, Toxapex can come in against Fighting-types that handle them such as Sneasler and Mega Staraptor. Additionally, Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot complement Toxapex by making it much more troublesome to remove.

  • Garchomp removes Poison-types such as Mega Gengar and opposing Toxapex while also helping it handle threats such as Mega Delphox and Mega Raichu Y. Toxapex for its part can use Wide Guard to prevent Sinistcha and Mega Froslass from reliably threatening Garchomp with Matcha Gotcha and Blizzard. Wide Guard also allows Garchomp to use Earthquake without worrying about it hurting Toxapex.

  • Venusaur can pair well with Toxapex by scaring away Ground- and Water-types that cause Toxapex problems such as Garchomp, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-M with its Grass-type STAB moves. Meanwhile, Toxapex protects Venusaur from Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Mega Froslass's Blizzard with Wide Guard.

Prankster Support.description:
• Grimmsnarl utilizes its access to Prankster and dual screens to become a premier support Pokemon within Regulation M-B, supporting big threats like Archaludon and having a favorable type matchup against the likes of Basculegion-M and Garchomp.

  • Parting Shot: Thanks to Prankster, Parting Shot turns Grimmsnarl into a fast pivot option, allowing it to easily get out of sticky situations like a regular swap with the added benefit of lowering the opponent's offenses. Although it acts before most moves, Parting Shot does occur after players switch or Mega Evolve their Pokemon, allowing Grimmsnarl to bring in an ally weather setter on the same turn the opponent attempts to set up weather by one of the aforementioned methods.

  • Spirit Break versus Foul Play: Spirit Break allows Grimmsnarl to hit Dragon-types like Garchomp and Hydreigon hard while reducing the Special Attack of foes like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Floette, usually when they are switching in due to Grimmsnarl's low Speed. Spirit Break also deals significant damage to Mega Floette. Foul Play, on the other hand, is capable of OHKOing Basculegion-M and 2HKOing Mega Swampert and most Garchomp.

  • Light Clay: Thanks to Light Clay, partners like Archaludon and Gholdengo have more time to set up safely behind dual screens.

Other Options

  • Fake Out: Fake Out can be used over its attacking moves, allowing Grimmsnarl to provide further support by giving partners like Gholdengo an opportunity to set up. However, this leaves it vulnerable to moves like Taunt from Maushold.

  • Scary Face: Scary Face can be used over Spirit Break or Foul Play to grant Grimmsnarl an option of speed control, though it leaves Grimmsnarl entirely passive.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 14 Def / 20 SpD with Careful: The given SPs allow Grimmsnarl to survive Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M and, when Light Screen is set up, Moonblast from Mega Floette. The Defense SPs allow Grimmsnarl to always survive Dire Claw from Jolly Sneasler. A Calm nature can be run when using Foul Play to decrease damage from confusion and opposing Foul Play.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Steel-type Pokemon like Kingambit, Mega Metagross, Archaludon, and Gholdengo threaten Grimmsnarl with Iron Head, Flash Cannon, and Make It Rain. Kingambit can switch in on Spirit Break to activate Defiant, while Gholdengo is immune to Parting Shot and can use Nasty Plot to offset the Special Attack drops from Spirit Break, which does minimal damage to it.

  • Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten huge damage onto Grimmsnarl through dual screens, especially against sets without Spirit Break.

  • Farigiraf, thanks to Armor Tail, denies Parting Shot and, if it's run, Scary Face from affecting Farigiraf's allies, severely hindering Grimmsnarl's effectiveness.

  • Fake Out from the likes of Sneasler and Incineroar prevent Grimmsnarl from setting up dual screens, leaving it vulnerable to another attack like Moonblast from Mega Floette. Sneasler itself threatens huge damage onto Grimmsnarl with Dire Claw, while Incineroar is immune to Prankster moves and easily tanks any attacks that Grimmsnarl carries.

  • Outside of pressuring a few select targets like Basculegion-M, Grimmsnarl struggles to carry an offensive presence on the field, leaving itself to be rather easily ignored.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Offensive partners like Gholdengo are recommended to offset Grimmsnarl's passivity. Gholdengo is able to threaten Fairy-types and walls out Farigiraf and Sneasler, as well as having a good matchup against Mega Metagross without Stomping Tantrum. Archaludon fills this role well as well, acting as a bulkier partner that exchanges Gholdengo's good Fairy-type matchup for a better matchup against physical attackers like Kingambit thanks to a combination of Reflect and Stamina.

  • Mega Staraptor threatens Steel-types with Close Combat. In return, Grimmsnarl not only provides dual screens but can also use Parting Shot on Mega Staraptor to make it even stronger thanks to Contrary. Grimmsnarl can also use Spirit Break to offset boosts granted to opposing Archaludon by Electro Shot, allowing Mega Staraptor to feel less threatened.

  • Sinistcha creates a strong supportive core alongside Grimmsnarl, healing up common partners behind dual screens and allowing them to easily set up and sweep games.

  • Mega Swampert can use Earthquake or High Horsepower to hit Steel-types, Sneasler, and Incineroar hard while also threatening big damage onto the format's Fairy-types with Wave Crash. Grimmsnarl, in return, can easily pivot to Pelipper against opposing weather setters with Parting Shot. Archaludon also appreciates this to become a dangerous sweeper thanks to the combination of dual screens, Stamina, (AC) and Electro Shot.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Basculegion-M aims to punch holes early in the game, using Wave Crash to chunk and KO threats like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Aerodactyl. It can then clean up late-game with Last Respects, outspeeding and breaking through opposing late-game sweepers like Mega Floette and Gholdengo.

  • Last Respects: Last Respects is what turns Basculegion-M into one of the scariest threats in Regulation M-B, easily OHKOing foes like Gholdengo at 100 Base Power and Mega Floette at 150 Base Power.

  • Flip Turn: Flip Turn allows Basculegion-M to easily pivot out, dealing chip damage to put foes like Mega Tyranitar and Sylveon in range of Wave Crash and 100-Base Power Last Respects.

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Basculegion-M to outspeed foes like Mega Froslass and Sneasler.

  • Adaptability: Adaptability allows Basculegion-M to OHKO non-Kasib Berry Sinistcha with 100-Base Power Last Respects.

Teambuilding

========

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Grass-type Pokemon like Mega Venusaur can easily tank Wave Crash, while non-Mega Venusaur can outspeed and threaten to OHKO Basculegion-M with Solar Beam when in the sun. Whimsicott and Sinistcha can use Tailwind and Trick Room, respectively, to allow partners like Gholdengo and Mega Staraptor to outspeed and threaten Basculegion-M with Shadow Ball and Brave Bird, respectively.

  • Toxapex can easily swap in on Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks and punish Basculegion-M with Baneful Bunker. Other bulky Water-type Pokemon like Mega Blastoise and Rotom-Wash also give Basculegion-M trouble, hitting it with Dark Pulse and Thunderbolt, respectively. Milotic, after setting up Coil a couple of times, can safely put Basculegion-M to sleep with Hypnosis and either chip it down with Muddy Water or allow partners like Kingambit to OHKO it.

  • Kingambit can tank Wave Crash and OHKO Basculegion-M with Kowtow Cleave or even use Sucker Punch to deal huge damage to it before it can move. Hydreigon also causes issues, resisting all of Basculegion-M's attacks and retaliating with Dark Pulse or outspeeding and KOing it thanks to its own Choice Scarf.

  • Trick Room is an issue for Basculegion-M, exploiting the Choice Scarf to make it move last; slower Pokemon like Kingambit that already threaten Basculegion-M become even more threatening. Tailwind similarly allows otherwise slower Pokemon like Mega Floette to outspeed and OHKO Basculegion-M with Light of Ruin.

  • Because of Basculegion-M's Choice Scarf, it becomes very easy to exploit; when Basculegion-M is locked into Last Respects, Normal-type Pokemon like Farigiraf can easily chunk it down with Thunderbolt, but when Basculegion-M is locked into Wave Crash, the aforementioned Water- and Grass-type Pokemon as well as Dragon-type Pokemon, like Mega Dragonite, become far scarier.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Kingambit deters Trick Room thanks to its low Speed, threatens opposing Ghost-type Pokemon like Basculegion-M with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch, and hits opposing Kingambit hard with Low Kick. Sneasler can hit opposing Dark-type Pokemon hard while also doing well against Venusaur that don't carry Earth Power and Whimsicott thanks to Dire Claw. Sneasler can also form a potent combination with Basculegion-M, threatening the Normal-type Pokemon that annoy it with Close Combat. Both Kingambit and Sneasler appreciate the support against opposing Sneasler and Mega Aerodactyl, respectively. Garchomp can easily switch in on Thunderbolt from Rotom-Wash and hits foes like Toxapex hard with Earthquake.

  • Mega Charizard Y can OHKO Grass-type Pokemon like Venusaur that give Basculegion-M trouble while using Solar Beam to deal with Water-types, gaining an extra layer of support against Rock-type Pokemon in return. Basculegion-M also provides good coverage against opposing Fire-type Pokemon like Mega Delphox and Mega Charizard Y, which Mega Floette greatly appreciates. To return the favor, Mega Floette hits Dragon- and Dark-type Pokemon hard.

  • Whimsicott and Grimmsnarl both help against opposing speed control; Whimsicott helps match Tailwind and lock Trick Room users into Trick Room with Encore, while Grimmsnarl sets up dual screens, allowing Basculegion-M to survive otherwise lethal attacks like Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Both also have access to Fairy-type STAB moves, while Basculegion-M helps out against the aforementioned Fire-type Pokemon as well as Gholdengo.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Annihilape uses its excellent offensive coverage, solid Speed, and immunity to common defensive tools like Intimidate and Fake Out to dismantle opposing teams and create awkward situations for the opponent with Phantom Force. It also has incredible matchups against metagame staples like Incineroar, Sneasler, and Kingambit.

  • Phantom Force: Phantom Force forces common setup Pokemon like Mega Delphox, Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar to either switch out or take devastating damage. Phantom Force also breaks Protect, which can allow a slower partner to attack Annihilape's target even if they use Protect.

  • Rock Tomb vs. Rage Fist: Rock Tomb can be used for speed control and allows Annihilape to deal big damage to Mega Charizard Y. Rage Fist can be used as an alternate Ghost-type attack. Its damage output is slightly higher than Phantom Force after Annihilape gets hit once, and at 150 Base Power, Rage Fist can OHKO Sinistcha, Gholdengo, and Sneasler.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash is needed to let Annihilape check Pokemon like Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar that could otherwise outspeed and OHKO it with moves like Psychic and Shadow Ball respectively.

  • Defiant: Defiant makes Annihilape great at deterring Intimidate users. When combined with Annihilape's Fake Out immunity and Close Combat, it makes Annihilape a perfect counter to Incineroar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fast Fairy-types like Mega Floette, Whimsicott, and Sylveon under Tailwind can 2HKO Annihilape while tanking a Phantom Force or Rage Fist. Mega Staraptor can similarly outspeed and threaten Annihilape with Brave Bird while also being able to tank any of its attacks; however, it can take big damage from Phantom Force or a boosted Rage Fist combined with Brave Bird's recoil. Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed and OHKO Annihilape through its Focus Sash with Dual Wingbeat.

  • Redirection: Maushold and Mega Scovillain are particularly bad redirectors for Annihilape to deal with. Maushold can nullify Phantom Force's damage due to its Ghost immunity, while Mega Scovillain can burn Annihilape thanks to Spicy Spray, which not only reduces Annihilape's offensive prowess but also breaks its Focus Sash.

  • Farigiraf: Farigiraf can safely switch into Phantom Force while also being able to tank a Close Combat. Farigiraf can also remove Annihilape's Speed advantage with Trick Room and 2HKO it with Psychic.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is one of Annihilape's best partners due to its Fairy resistance and ability to deal big damage to Annihilape's checks. Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave ignores redirection and can 2HKO Maushold and Mega Scovillain, while Weather Ball can 2HKO Farigiraf through its Sitrus Berry healing. In return, Annihilape can force out Basculegion-M and Incineroar, which are common checks to Mega Charizard Y.

  • Poison-types: With Chlorophyll, Venusaur in the sun can outspeed and threaten Fairy-types with Sludge Bomb. If given a Life Orb, it can outspeed and OHKO Mega Aerodactyl with Solar Beam. Toxapex can sit in front of Fairy-types and take them down over time with the combination of Toxic and Infestation. Toxapex can also trap Pokemon on the field with Infestation, forcing them to get hit by Phantom Force. Phantom Force combined with Protect can let Annihilape stall out turns, letting Toxapex's Infestation and Toxic rack up damage before Phantom Force KOes the target.

  • Incineroar and Garchomp: Incineroar can use Fake Out to let Annihilape set up a Phantom Force and can threaten Farigiraf with Throat Chop. Intimidate also drops Mega Aerodactyl's Attack low enough so that it can't OHKO Annihilape with Dual Wingbeat. Incineroar appreciates Annihilape's good matchups against Sneasler and Basculegion-M. Choice Scarf Garchomp can outspeed and deal big damage to Mega Aerodactyl with Rock Slide, and it appreciates Annihilape's ability to threaten Hydreigon.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Kingambit is one of the top threats of Regulation M-B, trading damage comfortably and threatening many top threats such as Basculegion-M, Gholdengo, and Mega Floette. Additionally, Kingambit's typing allows it to defensively answer both Gholdengo's and Mega Metagross's STAB moves as well as making it immune to Toxapex's Toxic.

  • Items: Black Glasses allows Kingambit to deal more damage with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch always OHKOes Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and can OHKO Mega Froslass in the snow most of the time. Focus Sash allows Kingambit to sacrifice its defenses to patch up its lackluster Speed, and it enables Kingambit to survive strong attacks such as Mega Floette's Light of Ruin, Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, and Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball. Focus Sash Kingambit is utilized on Tailwind teams to take advantage of any Speed investment. Chople Berry lets Kingambit retain its great bulk and utilize Trick Room better while surviving Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat, Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar, and Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast. Chople Berry Kingambit can also survive Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, but this isn't guaranteed.

  • Abilities: Defiant allows Kingambit to punish Incineroar's and Staraptor's Intimidate, Milotic's Icy Wind, and even the Special Attack drops from Mega Floette's and Whimsicott's Moonblast. Defiant's boost lets Kingambit always OHKO Sinistcha with Kowtow Cleave.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch makes up for Kingambit's poor Speed and threatens faster Pokemon such as Basculegion-M. Sucker Punch is also useful for late-game one-on-ones, as it pressures the opponent to guess whether Kingambit will choose Kowtow Cleave or Sucker Punch.

  • Iron Head versus Swords Dance versus Low Kick: Iron Head is used to threaten Mega Floette and Sylveon while dealing decent damage to Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and chunking Tyranitar. Swords Dance turns Kingambit into a setup sweeper; it's typically seen with Black Glasses to add another damage multiplier. A Black Glasses- and Swords Dance-boosted Sucker Punch can OHKO frailer Mega Charizard Y and Garchomp. Low Kick is used to threaten opposing Kingambit, Incineroar, and Tyranitar. However, Kingambit cannot damage Fairy-types or Sneasler much if it opts for Low Kick.

  • Protect versus Low Kick: Low Kick is an alternative coverage move if Kingambit doesn't necessarily need Protect on its team. This comes at the cost of Kingambit being unable to shield itself from Fake Out and attacks that may threaten it. Focus Sash and Chople Berry are typically seen with this option, because it allows Kingambit to trade damage more comfortably.

Other Options

  • Life Orb: Life Orb pushes Kingambit's power to the absolute limit, at the cost of some recoil. A Life Orb-boosted Sucker Punch OHKOes some Gholdengo.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def with Adamant: This is Kingambit's primary SP spread. Chople Berry and Black Glasses are typically seen with this spread.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread is used with a set utilizing four attacks and Focus Sash, allowing Kingambit to outspeed bulkier Pelipper and some Incineroar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Even with Chople Berry, Kingambit does not have the best matchup against Sneasler and Mega Staraptor. Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar threaten to OHKO Kingambit as well, and without speed control, Tyranitar will beat Black Glasses Kingambit. Despite Kingambit's ability acting as a check to Incineroar's Intimidate, its Flare Blitz still threatens Kingambit.

  • Without Iron Head or a Swords Dance boost, Mega Floette and Sylveon will outlast Kingambit in damage trades. Additionally, Mega Floette's Light of Ruin will OHKO non-Focus Sash Kingambit.

  • Mega Charizard Y is faster than Kingambit and will threaten to OHKO it, while Excadrill, Mega Swampert, and Garchomp are Ground-types that threaten Kingambit super effectively while also outspeeding it.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M and Sinistcha can block Sneasler's Close Combat, and the former can OHKO Sneasler with Wave Crash while resisting Dire Claw. Furthermore, Basculegion-M also threatens Incineroar for huge damage even with Intimidate. Sinistcha can set up Trick Room for Kingambit, allowing Kingambit to outspeed and beat threats to Sinistcha, such as non-Focus Sash Basculegion and Mega Froslass.

  • Sneasler can threaten opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar with Close Combat and provide Fake Out support so that Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance safely. Kingambit can deal with Gholdengo and Mega Metagross in return.

  • Mega Charizard Y can support Kingambit teams with its immunity to Garchomp's Earthquake and resistance to Incineroar's Flare Blitz, opposing Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Mega Staraptor's Close Combat while pressuring opposing Kingambit and Mega Scovillain. In return, Kingambit can cover Mega Aerodactyl for it.

  • Garchomp can threaten opposing Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Tyranitar. Kingambit boasts an excellent matchup against Mega Froslass, as well as Alolan Ninetales if it is running Iron Head, both of which Garchomp usually struggles with. However, Garchomp cannot safely use Earthquake next to Kingambit.

  • Mega Floette and Sylveon can threaten opposing Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Mega Staraptor. Their weakness to Poison-type moves such as Sneasler's Poison Jab and Venusaur's Sludge Bomb is in turn patched up by Kingambit's Steel typing.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Gholdengo, thanks to its naturally strong defensive typing, easily walls out common Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and helps beat top Pokemon like Mega Floette, Sylveon, Mega Aerodactyl, and Sinistcha. This typing allows Gholdengo to set up Nasty Plot, letting it sweep through teams with its STAB moves and threaten nearly all metagame staples with at least neutral damage.

  • Make It Rain: Make It Rain hits nearly anything that doesn't resist it for huge damage after a Nasty Plot, having a solid chance to OHKO Mega Tyranitar with Life Orb. When using Make It Rain, Gholdengo must be careful; using it at the wrong time late-game will leave Gholdengo too weak to contribute much . This forces Gholdengo to use Nasty Plot again and leave itself or its partner open to attacks.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb gives Gholdengo potential for large amounts of burst damage, allowing Gholdengo to OHKO most Mega Froslass with Make It Rain and Basculegion-M with Shadow Ball, though it comes at the cost of Gholdengo's longevity. For this reason, builds that use Life Orb Gholdengo tend to run faster and more offensive SP spreads to turn it into a strong and threatening attacker that doesn't require setup turns.

  • Spell Tag and Metal Coat: Spell Tag and Metal Coat save Gholdengo's longevity but only allow it to boost either Shadow Ball or Make it Rain. Spell Tag allows Gholdengo to 2HKO Sneasler, while Metal Coat allows Gholdengo to OHKO Mega Aerodactyl.

  • Good as Gold: Good as Gold gives Gholdengo good chances to switch into attacks like Parting Shot from Incineroar and Grimmsnarl as well as Sleep Powder from Venusaur.

Other Options

  • Leftovers: Leftovers allow Gholdengo to focus more on setting up by increasing its longevity, though the item sacrifices power.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 8 Def / 7 SpA / 3 SpD / 16 Spe with Timid: The given SP spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Adamant Basculegion-M, almost always survive Earthquake from Jolly Life Orb Garchomp, and withstand Dark Pulse from Mega Blastoise, with the rest dumped into Special Attack.

  • 7 HP / 32 SpA / 27 Spe with Timid: This SP spread is tailored towards Life Orb sets. It lets Gholdengo outrun Jolly Basculegion-M and survive Wave Crash from Choice Scarf Adamant Basculegion-M, allowing Gholdengo to retaliate with Shadow Ball. The remaining SPs are put into Special Attack.

  • 17 HP / 1 Def / 15 SpA / 1 SpD / 32 Spe with Modest: With the SPs in HP, Defense, and Special Defense, Gholdengo can possibly survive Flare Blitz from Incineroar and has a high chance to survive Heat Wave from Timid Mega Delphox. The SPs in Special Attack allow Life Orb-boosted Shadow Ball to OHKO Mega Delphox and +2 Make It Rain to OHKO uninvested Mega Tyranitar, which typically uses Dragon Dance sets. The Speed SPs allow Gholdengo to outspeed all Mega Tyranitar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-type Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Blaziken, Incineroar, and Mega Scovillain threaten huge damage onto Gholdengo with Heat Wave, Weather Ball, Flare Blitz, and Overheat. Incineroar in particular resists both of Gholdengo's STAB options, tanking Make It Rain and Shadow Ball and retaliating with Throat Chop or Flare Blitz.

  • Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar outspeed and threaten to OHKO Gholdengo with Last Respects and Shadow Ball. Hydreigon, Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar are Dark-types that OHKO Gholdengo with Dark Pulse, Kowtow Cleave, and Knock Off. Additionally, Hydreigon can opt for Snarl instead to slowly chip down Gholdengo and weaken it in the process, and Kingambit can use Sucker Punch to hit Gholdengo before it moves.

  • Ground-types like Mega Swampert and Garchomp threaten Gholdengo with Earthquake. Mega Swampert also resists Make It Rain and is placed on rain teams alongside Pokemon like Hydreigon and Archaludon, which can deal lots of damage to Gholdengo with Dark Pulse and Electro Shot. On the other hand, Garchomp's flexibility enables it to fit on many teams, meaning that it is a hurdle that Gholdengo often has to face.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp threatens Fire-types aside from Mega Scovillain with Earthquake, and it can handle Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide.

  • Incineroar and Kingambit can switch into Ghost-types and threaten them with Throat Chop and Kowtow Cleave, while Sneasler and Mega Staraptor can help Gholdengo handle Dark-types with Close Combat.

  • Sinistcha can heal up Gholdengo with Hospitality and redirect many attacks with Rage Powder; it can also switch into Ground-types and threaten Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha. Alolan Ninetales can threaten Ground-types with Freeze-Dry and Blizzard.
